PREPARATION COST Austin pays fire cadets
Paid cadet academy Austin Fire Department hired cadets; not every Texas fire school
Cost details & what’s extra
Austin recruits cadets into a paid academy that prepares them for firefighter and EMT certification. Selection and available positions apply. A separate self-funded fire school is a different route.
Checked 2026-10-16. Published reference.

More info · salary sources
Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos, TX · Austin Fire entry reviewed October 18, 2026; 2025 occupation wages for later scenarios. These figures show employee pay, not a business’s sales. Source years are preserved; future inflation and promotions are not added.
Starting pay is Austin Fire’s published post-academy amount. Later scenarios use the local occupation benchmark, with starting pay as their minimum. Later planning amounts move 45%, 75%, and 100% of the gap toward the occupation’s experienced-wage benchmark, subject to the starting-pay floor and local wage bounds. TWC’s experienced wage is the mean of the upper-paid two-thirds; where suppressed, the sourced local median is used. These fractions are planning assumptions, not a fitted experience-year series.
Later rounded amounts are similar because the wage benchmark or starting-pay floor is close across these stages. No raise is added just to make the chart rise.
Paid training source: Public recruiting page reviewed October 18, 2026; salary effective date not stated · checked 2026-10-18.
Employee wage estimates exclude self-employed workers, unincorporated owners, and business profit.
TWC entry proxy is the mean of the lowest-paid third, not observed pay at a particular year. Experience scenarios are separate editorial assumptions.
Assumes growing proficiency in the same public-service role. Does not assume promotion or a different professional license.
Figures hold purchasing power constant. No future inflation is added. Future labor-market conditions and personal outcomes can differ.
Entry means a first full-time qualified job after required preparation. Experience years begin there; education and apprenticeship years are separate.
Austin Fire entry is the $67,999 amount published when checked October 18, 2026; the page does not state its effective date. Later scenarios combine the 2025 local occupation benchmark with this entry floor. The occupational experienced-wage anchor remains $67,726 and is not an employer service schedule.
Cadet and post-academy pay ↗
· Austin Fire Department · checked 2026-10-18 · Public recruiting page reviewed October 18, 2026; salary effective date not stated Published $67,999 probationary entry after successful academy completion; later amounts are planning scenarios with that entry floor.

· U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics via O*NET OnLine Local wage anchor; all experience ratios are Fieldguide assumptions.
How to use occupational wages ↗
· U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Wage variation guidance; does not publish experience-year estimates.
Entry and experienced wage definitions ↗
· Texas Workforce Commission Entry is the mean of the lowest-paid third; experienced is the mean of the upper-paid two-thirds. These groups are not years of experience.
Published experienced-wage anchor ↗
· Texas Workforce Commission Average of the upper-paid two-thirds; not measured pay at a particular experience year.
